tests_conducted.hypothesis_statement: There is a statistically significant difference in voluntary 90-day churn rate between paid_search and organic acquisition channels, with paid_search higher, in the Q3 cohort.
tests_conducted.null_hypothesis: Voluntary 90-day churn rate is equal between paid_search and organic acquisition channels.
tests_conducted.alternative_hypothesis: Voluntary 90-day churn rate is higher for paid_search than for organic acquisition channels.
tests_conducted.test_selected: Two-proportion z-test (one-sided), with Cramér's V for effect size from the full 5×3 contingency table
tests_conducted.test_selection_reasoning: Outcome is binary (churned/retained) and the predictor is a discrete channel; the channel cohorts are independent samples. n is large (paid_search ~12k, organic ~17k) so the normal approximation is valid. Cramér's V from χ² gives a channel-level effect size that scales with the multi-channel comparison Phase 4 visualised.
tests_conducted.practical_significance_reasoning: A 17-percentage-point absolute gap in voluntary churn between paid_search (31%) and organic (14%) is well above any plausible measurement noise and large enough to justify a channel-specific retention intervention.

tests_conducted.hypothesis_statement: There is a statistically significant negative association between event_count_30d and 90-day voluntary churn among users acquired in Q2 2025.
tests_conducted.null_hypothesis: log(event_count_30d) is not associated with the log-odds of voluntary 90-day churn.
tests_conducted.alternative_hypothesis: log(event_count_30d) is negatively associated with the log-odds of voluntary 90-day churn.
tests_conducted.test_selected: Logistic regression on log(event_count_30d + 1); Mann-Whitney U as non-parametric confirmation
tests_conducted.test_selection_reasoning: Outcome is binary, predictor is heavily right-skewed (Phase 4 univariate showed median 12 / mean 47), so a log transform plus logistic regression is the standard approach. Mann-Whitney U adds a distribution-free check that the medians differ.
tests_conducted.practical_significance_reasoning: Each ~2.7× increase in first-30-day event count cuts the odds of voluntary churn by 34%. That is a directly actionable lever — even a modest onboarding lift to median engagement would reduce voluntary churn meaningfully.

tests_conducted.hypothesis_statement: There is a statistically significant increase in weekly voluntary churn rate after 2025-07-15 vs the matching pre-period in the same Q3 cohort.
tests_conducted.null_hypothesis: The post-2025-07-15 weekly voluntary churn rate equals the pre-period rate after seasonal adjustment.
tests_conducted.alternative_hypothesis: Post-2025-07-15 weekly voluntary churn rate exceeds the seasonally-adjusted pre-period rate.
tests_conducted.test_selected: Segmented (interrupted) regression with 2024 Q3 weekly churn as the seasonal control series
tests_conducted.test_selection_reasoning: Pre/post difference confounded with seasonality — a naive t-test would inflate the effect. Segmented regression with a control series isolates the change-point shift from seasonal drift. We treat 2024 Q3 as the seasonal baseline.
tests_conducted.practical_significance_reasoning: A ~44% relative bump in weekly voluntary churn is meaningful but the underpowered series (only 12 weekly post-points) means the magnitude estimate is uncertain. Practical significance is real but the size is calibrated MEDIUM not HIGH until a longer post-window is available.

tests_conducted.hypothesis_statement: There is a statistically significant interaction between acquisition_channel and event_count_30d in predicting voluntary churn (the engagement→retention slope is steeper for paid_search than for referral).
tests_conducted.null_hypothesis: The interaction term channel × log(events) has coefficient 0 in a logistic model predicting voluntary churn.
tests_conducted.alternative_hypothesis: The interaction term is non-zero, with a steeper negative slope for paid_search than for referral.
tests_conducted.test_selected: Logistic regression with channel × log(events) interaction term
tests_conducted.test_selection_reasoning: Direct test of the multivariate pattern surfaced in Phase 4. Logistic regression supports both the main-effect estimates and the interaction term with comparable confidence intervals.
tests_conducted.practical_significance_reasoning: Channel-targeted onboarding lift would help paid_search more than referral, but the absolute slope-difference is modest. Worth a targeted experiment, not yet a full programme.

statistical_caveats: All findings are observational, not experimental — channel-level differences may reflect confounding with user intent rather than channel causation.
H3 (pricing-change effect) is supported but UNDERPOWERED on the post-window (12 weeks); magnitude estimate is provisional and should be re-tested at the 6-month mark.
Holm–Bonferroni correction at family-wise α=0.05 across 4 hypotheses; all survive — no Type I inflation concern.
Phase 3 bias_audit flagged regex-standardisation of cancel_reason; voluntary-churn rates may be slightly inflated. Direction of bias is conservative for H1 (so result holds a fortiori).
phase_6_priority_insights: H1 + H2 are independently HIGH-significance and combine into the single most actionable finding: low-engagement paid_search users are the dominant churn driver.
H3's pricing-change effect needs a root-cause look at whether it shows up uniformly across plan tiers or concentrates on starter (which would link it to the 'first-bill cliff' Phase 4 anomaly).
H4's interaction effect makes onboarding investment channel-targeted — Phase 6 should quantify the expected lift if paid_search engagement is brought to organic's median.
